newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals except for gold end firmer.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals except for gold end firmer.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures except for gold ended firmer on Thursday, buoyed by firmer bullion prices, while gold futures failed to end in positive territory following steep losses in New York overnight, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from flat to six yen per gram lower, with most-active benchmark February ending down three at 1,373 yen.
In gold futures, private investors continued to hunt for bargains, while trade houses sold gold futures on seeing the yen's firmer tendency, the traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted firmer at $341.90/342.40 per ounce at 0742 GMT, lifted by short-covering, against $341.00/50 in New York on Wednesday.
"Bearish sentiment remains intact," one trader said. The possibility of German gold sales also dampened sentiment, traders said.
"In gold futures, private investors may hunt for bargains below the 1,380 yen level, but they would be quick to take profits when the benchmark approaches 1,400 yen," they said.
Local investors, who bought gold and sold platinum earlier due to the widening spread, switched to buying platinum.
